premise.dramatic_question: Will {HERO} and {COMPANION} follow {ANCESTOR}'s {BROADCAST} all the way to {GOAL} before {DEADLINE}, and decide what becomes of it once they are standing in the room?
resolution_space: frost on the high way turns a climb into a hand on a jacket and a ride home with the hunt intact
a weak floor gives, an arm catches, and the two of them name the risk honestly on the way out
an old reel is threaded instead of hunted, and one shared showing is worth the rest of the night
an unfit shortcut on the water swamps in a boot's depth and buys nothing but wet socks and a rule remembered
cocoa and an adult's stories outlast the clock, and the club comes alive in the telling instead of in a cache
an untried handle wakes the night noise-maker, and the children stand still and answer for themselves
a loose slope walks out from under them and the long way up is still there tomorrow
an overreach at the destination's window is hauled back by a sibling, and nobody breaks into what is theirs anyway
one caption too many at the wall, and the sign-off happens while they are still reading, heard but unanswered
the last broadcast is witnessed from the steps through the door, unopened and entirely enough
an answer spoken into the pause draws old voices back out of the static, one check-in at a time
an answer spoken, a name signed under the elder's own, and the tape closed with family at both ends
the club's closing words read exactly as written, and the watch ends precisely as it was built to end
the closing words read, then one promise added, and the machine wound for one more year
hands shaken over a wound spring, and the station has keepers again
a plan built out of diagrams and uncrossed names turns finders into a properly trained crew
a phone call before the end, and three generations standing in front of the desk for the last groups
five new groups recorded in the children's own voices, and the hunt handed to the town's next finders

label_styles: imperative and verb-first: what we do next, said out loud
name the place you are going to, let the reason stay implied
one trailing adverb where the choice has a mood: quietly, first, anyway
short sentences closed with a full stop, never a question mark
physical verbs for physical legs, quiet verbs for the choices about people

safety_envelope.affect_ceiling: night-time wonder with mild, bounded suspense; the dark is company, not threat, and urgency may tighten but never tips into fear for anyone's safety

code_forms.note: BOUND ONCE, USED THROUGHOUT. One code form per story, chosen at bind and rendered the same way every time it appears: the groups copied at n_start, the key applied at n_decode, each site's own hint group at wt_gate, cn_marquee, hb_shed, lb_green and bh_wind, and the five-word closing phrase read at f_answer_script and spoken at e_win_signoff. A reader who learns it in the kitchen can follow it at every site and recognize it at the end.

waypoint_marks.note: BOUND ONCE, USED THROUGHOUT. The elder's personal waypoint mark, one per story, rendered the same wherever it recurs: the logbook margins, wt_marks, cn_horns, hb_doors, hb_cage, hb_pad, lb_maproom, lb_hunt, bh_plate, bh_pillar. It is the reader's proof of a single hand behind the whole night.

site_landmarks.note: one per branch off the hub, drawn freely but unique within the story; each must be somewhere a town kid can reach by bike at night, look around inside, and leave from safely

destination_building.note: the small building east of town the bearing points to all night; small, warm, and plainly kept up by one person

cache_containers.note: one hiding place per site, unique within the story; every one is inert, dry and safe to open, and each is hidden by wit rather than by lock

keepsake_tokens.note: one per site cache; each carries a single word, and the five words in site order assemble the closing phrase read at the end. They are keepsakes, never valuables

memory_slips.note: one per site cache; each hands over one first-hand memory of the elder among her club and closes with the story's refrain, so any single site teaches who she was

club_relics.note: the incidental proofs, scattered across the sites and the destination, that the club was a real community of working people: one at wt_photo, one at hb_pad, one at lb_table, one at fin_wall

retreat_obstacles.note: one per site plus one at the destination, unique within the story; each must be visibly retreatable and cost only time, dignity, a scrape or a soaking, never safety

night_keepers.note: the two named adults who belong to their own sites: kind, firm about the rules, glad to be asked, and never the reason the night goes wrong

wonder_details.note: one sensory marvel per site, drawn freely; the thing a reader remembers about that place after the clue is solved

key_hiding_places.note: where the destination's key waits; it must read as left for a finder, so entering is inheritance and never breaking in

station_workings.note: the machinery that makes the broadcast run itself and makes keeping it possible; every piece must be understandable by a twelve-year-old in one look

affect.target: hair-raising wonder at a familiar voice arriving from nowhere

code_form.note: the story's one code form; every later coded beat renders this same form, so the reader can learn it here and use it all night

receiver.note: the inherited set that wakes itself; benign, hand-sized, and plainly old
